body:
This is mostly @akien-mga / @Repiteo 's area as they make the builds.

Afaik an internal compiler error is reporting a compiler bug, rather than an engine bug _per se_. As I understand it, it may be _indirectly_ caused by a bug in the source code, but a compiler working correctly should never be reporting internal compiler errors.

The version of MinGW may be crucial, I gather we had to downgrade to a previous version because of a compiler bug. It will be worth mentioning which versions of all the toolchains you are using and checking they are as used in the official builds.

Especially note we moved to c++17 with 3.7, so there is no guarantee that a toolchain that worked with 3.5 will still work with 3.7.

If you can post a version of the debug template errors, that might be helpful.

Yes this is likely a GCC bug, which may be fixed in newer versions (you seem to have mingw-gcc 13.3.0).

We had no issue building Windows binaries with LTO for 3.6.2-stable and 3.7-dev1 using Fedora 43's mingw-gcc (MinGW 13.0.0 with GCC 15.2.1): https://github.com/godotengine/build-containers/tree/3.6?tab=readme-ov-file#toolchains
But we actually had a crashing build when compiling 3.6.2-stable with Fedora 42's mingw-gcc (MinGW 12.0.0 with GCC 14.2.1). Especially when using LTO, mingw-gcc versions can easily run into bugs with Godot's complex codebase.

Since you can't reproduce it in 3.5 and earlier, it does mean that a Godot change triggered the GCC bug, so bisecting it could also be useful to see if we can work it around. But otherwise the solution would likely be to update to the latest mingw-gcc.

Here's what Grok has to say, sounds like that version of MinGW is pretty broken:
<details>
The errors you’re seeing are not Godot bugs — they are GCC internal compiler errors (ICE) happening very late in the compilation, during Link-Time Optimization (LTO) with a MinGW-w64 cross-compiler (GCC 15.2.1 in your case).

### Key Parts of the Log

internal compiler error: in binds_to_current_def_p, at symtab.cc:2598

This is a classic GCC ICE in the symbol table handling when LTO is enabled.It happens in multiple unrelated files (translation.h, compressed_translation.h, joints_2d_sw.cpp, even in the standard library stl_uninitialized.h). This almost always means the compiler itself is crashing, not that the source code is wrong.The build is using full LTO (Using LTO: full) with MinGW-w64 and GCC 15.x. What This Almost Certainly MeansGCC 15.x (especially 15.0, 15.1 and early 15.2) has known, severe LTO bugs on the x86_64-w64-mingw32 target that trigger exactly this “binds_to_current_def_p” ICE when building large C++ projects like Godot.

Godot’s codebase is huge and stresses the compiler in ways most programs don’t, so it hits these bugs very reliably.These bugs are already reported upstream and many are fixed in GCC 15.2.1 or later, but the MinGW-w64 packages that ship GCC 15.2.1 in most distros (Arch, MSYS2, etc.) still contain the broken commits.How to Fix It (Practical Solutions That Work Right Now)Disable LTO completely (quickest and most reliable fix)

Run scons with:
```
scons target=release lto=full   →   change to   lto=none
```
_or_
```
scons target=release lto=thin
```
lto=thin sometimes works, lto=none always works and still gives perfectly fine performance for Godot Windows builds.
Use a known-good older or newer GCC version

Working versions for Godot Windows cross-compile right now (November 2025):GCC 14.2.0 (very stable with full LTO)
GCC 13.2 or 13.3
GCC 15.2.1 from the very latest MSYS2 packages (some people report it fixed after a recent update)

Bad versions: basically anything 15.0.0 → 15.2.0 and some early 15.2.1 builds.If you’re on Arch Linux, the current mingw-w64-gcc package is still broken for Godot with LTO. Either downgrade to 14.x or switch to MSYS2 and use their latest toolchain.

If you’re using MSYS2
Update everything and make sure you have the absolute latest:

```
pacman -Syu mingw-w64-x86_64-toolchain
```

Some users report that the November 2025 MSYS2 packages finally fixed this particular ICE.
Switch to Clang (also works very well for Godot Windows builds now)  

```
scons use_llvm=yes target=release
```

(you need mingw-w64-x86_64-clang installed)

### TL;DR
This is a known GCC 15.x + LTO bug on the MinGW target.

Just add lto=none (or lto=thin) to your scons command line and the build will finish instantly. You lose almost nothing in the final Windows binary performance.Example working command:

```
scons platform=windows target=release lto=none -j12
```

Once GCC 15.2.1+ is fully fixed in your distro’s MinGW package, you can re-enable lto=full if you really want the tiny extra optimization. For now, disabling LTO is the standard workaround used by virtually everyone cross-compiling Godot master for Windows.

</details>

Essentially, as the log indicates, this kind of bug is more important to be reported to the compiler writers (so they can fix it), rather than Godot (although it's helpful here to keep track of compiler bugs).

Sometimes there are things we can do to prevent a compiler bug manifesting, but there's a danger of degrading into a game of "whack-a-mole"...

We do a bunch of changes, they release a new version, which fix bugs we worked around, and introduces new bugs to whack.

So unless it's something obvious our side, it seems likely the best course of action is to advise on which versions _are known to work_ (presumably the same as those making the official builds).
